section_1.title: From Concrete to Abstract (1 minute)
section_1.content: Transition from familiar 2D/3D vectors (arrows) to the abstract concept. Introduce the core idea: a vector space is not defined by what its elements 'look' like, but by how they 'behave' under addition and scalar multiplication.
section_1.example: Visual: An arrow in 2D space transforms into a musical chord or a collection of photos. Even if they don't look like arrows, they follow the same 'algebraic rules'.

section_2.title: The 8 Rules of the Game (1.5 minutes)
section_2.content: Explain the 8 axioms of a vector space (Closure, Associativity, Commutativity, Identity, Inverse, Distributivity). Use a checklist visual to show that if a set satisfies these, it is a valid vector space.
section_2.example: Use a character named 'Vector-Bot' who checks if a mathematical object obeys these 8 rules. If one fails, the object is rejected.

section_3.title: Concrete vs. Abstract Examples (1.5 minutes)
section_3.content: Showcase that polynomials and functions function as vectors. Visualize the set of all polynomials of degree ≤ 2 as a space that can be mapped to 3D coordinate geometry.
section_3.example: Visual: A set of polynomials (e.g., ax² + bx + c) mapping to a 3D grid, showing that coefficients (a, b, c) act like coordinates (x, y, z).

section_4.title: Application and Conclusion (1 minute)
section_4.content: Briefly mention how abstract vector spaces are the backbone of modern tech, specifically Fourier transforms in audio processing or Hilbert spaces in Quantum Mechanics.
section_4.example: An audio signal from a cat meowing being broken down into a sum of sine waves—each sine wave is a vector in an infinite-dimensional space.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line.split("] ")[-1], font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.8 + j * 1.2

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
